subject: English
passage: When the Ming Dynasty porcelain vase, a piece purported to date to the early 1600s, appeared at auction in 2019, some collectors believed it demonstrated exceptional craftsmanship from China's golden age of ceramics. In 2022, a team including art historians Dr. Yue Qian and Dr. Valdis Ozols and materials scientist Dr. Siham Amrani performed a comprehensive analysis of the vase and the glazing technique used. They found that the glaze contains cobalt-60, a radioactive isotope that was first produced artificially in laboratories in the 1930s. Therefore, the team concluded that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: early 1600s Chinese artisans could not have created exceptional porcelain works.
choices.B: artisans must have used radioactive materials in their glazes in the 1600s.
choices.C: there isn't enough information to determine when the glaze was applied.
choices.D: the Ming Dynasty vase could not have been created by early 1600s craftsmen.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of Qian, Ozols, and Amrani's 2022 analysis of the Ming Dynasty vase. The text indicates that while some collectors believed the vase was created in the early 1600s, the 2022 analysis showed the presence of cobalt-60 in the glaze used on the vase. The text goes on to say that cobalt-60 wasn't produced until the 1930s, which means that glaze containing this isotope couldn't have been available to craftsmen in the 1600s. Since artisans in the early 1600s couldn't have used glaze with cobalt-60, it follows that the Ming Dynasty vase couldn't have been created by early 1600s craftsmen.
